[N004] Chief complaint: fever and spreading redness of the right lower leg for two days.
[N005] Vital signs: temperature 38.6 C, heart rate 104, blood pressure 132/78, respiratory rate 18, SpO2 97% on room air.
[N006] Allergies: NKDA.
[N007] Pain: 6/10, right lower leg.
[N008] Triage acuity: ESI 3. Placed in room 12 for provider evaluation.

QUESTION:
Summarize what this chart establishes about the patient's drug allergies.

ANSWER TO CHECK:
<<<
The chart documents a severe penicillin allergy: the active allergy list records anaphylaxis
(generalized hives, throat tightness, hypotension) after amoxicillin in May 2019, treated with
intramuscular epinephrine [A004, A005, A006]. The 2024 primary care note independently records
the same reaction and notes that no allergy testing has been done [C005, C006].

conflicts with the allergy list and the clinic note, and nothing in the record resolves it:
the allergy entry is still active and no entries have been removed [A006, A008]. The chart
therefore does not establish that the patient is free of drug allergies; it contains
conflicting documentation.

>>>
